title: Micro Mentee Pathway — 14-Day Activation Kit
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, low-friction onboarding + mentorship plan designed for early-career hires and internal transfers joining an engineering or product pod. The goal: make days 0–14 feel productive, reduce cognitive overhead, and create immediate mentor connections so the new hire ships a small, meaningful contribution by end of week two.

Audience
- Hiring manager
- Assigned mentor (buddy)
- New hire (mentees)
- People ops coordinator

Notes to self / context
- This doc is intentionally lightweight — good for remote hires and internal moves.
- Stacked with TODOs and quick templates so managers can copy/paste into Slack or Gmail.
- Links to more formal Playbooks (Confluence) at bottom.

High-level commitments (manager + mentor)
- Manager: clear first deliverable, 1:1 at day 1 and weekly thereafter, access + approvals done by day 0.
- Mentor: weekly 60 min shadow + 15 min daily standups first week, code review buddy for initial PRs.

Day 0 checklist (pre-first-day tasks for people ops + manager)
- Confirm account setup (OKTA, Google, GitHub, Slack) — people ops
- Provision dev machine or cloud access (VM creds) — infra
- Invite to pod Slack channels, calendar, docs — manager
- Send welcome note with day 1 agenda and pairing schedule — manager
- Prepare minimal 'first ticket' and a local dev walkthrough document — mentor

Day 1: orientation + low-friction wins
- 30 min 1:1 welcome (manager): role expectations, 14-day goal, team rituals.
- 60 min mentor pairing: repo clone, run local server, smoke test.
- Lunch intro (async or live) with pod.
- Assign first small ticket (README tweak, tiny bug, infra health check).
- Quick survey: how comfortable? blockers? (mentor sends Slack DM).

Days 2–5: embed + quick iteration
- Daily 15 min mentor check-ins (stand-up focused on blockers).
- First PR opened by day 3, review within 48 hours (mentor + reviewer).
- Shadow rotation: sit in on two async/code review sessions.
- Invite to weekly team ritual (planning, retro) if timing aligns.

Day 7 checkpoint (manager + mentor sync)
- 30 min check-in: review progress on first ticket, re-scope if necessary.
- Confirm access to internal docs, Confluence pages, and training playlists.
- Manager sets next milestone (feature or small spike) for days 8–14.

Days 8–14: own a tiny end-to-end feature
- Identify a scoped spike or small feature that results in a deployable change.
- Mentor reviews architecture decisions; manager checks alignment with roadmap.
- Aim for one merged PR and a retrospective note in team channel.

Sample first-ticket examples (pick one)
- Add a failing test that captures a bug and write the fix.
- Improve README or developer runbook (add missing env var steps).
- Small UI text fix or API input validation improvement.

Interview & hiring artifacts to keep continuity
- Include short hiring notes in the candidate file: top strengths, aptitude signals, 2 coaching points.
- Attach interview rubric snapshot used for hire (one-paragraph summary).

Mini interview rubric (for backfilling or internal portability)
- Signal: Problem solving (3 points) — did candidate break problem into steps?
- Signal: Communication (2 points) — clarity, asks clarifying Qs, sets expectations.
- Signal: Ownership fit (2 points) — demonstrated follow-through examples.
- Signal: Learning agility (3 points) — concrete examples of learning a new tool/stack.
- Quick guidance: keep rubric notes <= 6 bullet lines so future hiring managers actually read them.

Mentor playbook (quick)
- Day 1: hands-on repo walkthrough, run app locally.
- Day 2–5: focus on PR feedback & unblock.
- Day 7: architecture orientation (20–30 min).
- Day 10–14: pair on shipping and retrospective.
- Always: be explicit about expected response time in Slack.

Manager quick templates
- Welcome message (Slack): "Hi @newhire — welcome! Day 1 agenda: 10am 1:1, 11:30 pairing with @mentor. Ping me if anything blocks. — Ava"
- PR review SLA: "Aim to review mentee PRs within 48 hours. If delayed, ping the mentor to triage."

Acceptance & compliance checklist (HR)
- Signed offer returned, background check cleared.
- NDA & data access forms completed.
- Benefits enrollment window opened.

Measurement & success signals (first 30 days)
- Primary: merged PR owned by hire within 14 days.
- Secondary: first-week survey score >= 4/5 on clarity of next steps.
- Tertiary: mentor and manager satisfaction note added to employee file.

Escalation contacts
- People ops coordinator: "Sofia Ramirez" (Slack: @sofia, email: sofia@redwood.ai)
- Infra lead: "Marcus Li" (Slack: @marcus)
- Engineering manager oncall: provide team rota link in the hire packet.

Quick wins & anti-patterns
- Quick wins: scope very small deployable work, prioritize docs + tests over big features.
- Anti-patterns: expecting the hire to read 200 pages of docs before contributing, or assigning a large unknown feature as first task.

Templates and retro prompts (end of day 14)
- Retro prompt for hire: "What helped you onboard? What blocked you? One ask from your mentor/manager for next 30 days?"
- Manager retro prompt: "Was the first-ticket scope correct? Did mentor have capacity? Any access gaps to fix?"

Links & references
- Full Onboard Playbook: CONFLUENCE-ONBOARD-1482
- Hiring tracker: JIRA-HIRE-721
- Dev environment docs: GH-WIKI-DEVENV

Open items / TODOs
- Make a one-click onboarding checklist (Zapier/Asana) — people ops backlog.
- Add a short 3–5 min welcome video from the founder (asset request).
- Verify mentor load balancing logic for Q1 hires (data ask: mentor:mentee ratio).

Why this differs from other kits
- Focus on micro-deliverables and a mentor-first approach rather than a heavy week of courses.
- Explicit hiring-to-onboarding continuity: carry forward interview signals into the first 2 weeks to guide mentorship.

If anything is unclear, ping me — Ava.
